stories.original_title: Why I still reach for Lisp and Scheme instead of Haskell
stories.generated_headline: Malleability vs. Rigidity in Functional Paradigms
stories.summary: The enduring appeal of Lisp and Scheme lies in their radical 'softness'—the ability to hotfix production environments, reshape syntax via macros, and express complex domains without the friction of rigid type systems or the refactoring overhead required for simple tasks like print-debugging in Haskell. Quote: Scheme (and Lisp) allows you to express complex systems and problem domains in more simple terms than any other language can.
